tagline: Know your tools before you build with them

exam_gotcha: The Messages API uses 'assistant' role for Claude's responses, not 'ai' or 'claude'. Many questions test this.
key_concept: Model selection is an architectural decision — Haiku for speed/cost, Sonnet for balance, Opus for complex reasoning.

quiz_questions.q: Which Claude model family is optimized for speed and low cost?
quiz_questions.a: Haiku

quiz_questions.q: What is the role name used for Claude's responses in the Messages API?
quiz_questions.a: assistant

quiz_questions.q: What parameter controls the randomness of Claude's output?
quiz_questions.a: temperature

quiz_questions.q: What happens when max_tokens is reached before a natural stop?
quiz_questions.a: The response is truncated at that token limit with stop_reason 'max_tokens'

title: Prompt Engineering Deep Dive
tagline: The difference between a good prompt and a great one is architecture
subtopics: Zero-shot vs few-shot vs chain-of-thought prompting
XML tags for structure — why Claude responds well to them
Role prompting and persona assignment
Instruction ordering — Claude reads top-to-bottom, weight it accordingly
Avoiding prompt injection and adversarial inputs
Iterative prompt refinement methodology
Prompt chaining for complex tasks
exam_gotcha: Claude is trained to follow instructions in order of specificity. System prompt > human turn. Later instructions in the same turn can override earlier ones.
key_concept: XML tags (<example>, <instructions>, <context>) are not just aesthetic — they help Claude segment information and follow structure reliably.

quiz_questions.q: Which prompting technique asks Claude to show its reasoning before giving a final answer?
quiz_questions.a: Chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting

quiz_questions.q: Which has higher priority: system prompt instructions or user turn instructions?
quiz_questions.a: System prompt instructions take precedence

quiz_questions.q: What HTML-like syntax does Claude respond especially well to for structured prompts?
quiz_questions.a: XML tags

quiz_questions.q: What is few-shot prompting?
quiz_questions.a: Providing examples of input-output pairs in the prompt to guide Claude's response format

title: System Prompts & Context Management
tagline: Context is the canvas. You decide what Claude sees.
subtopics: System prompt architecture — what belongs there vs the human turn
Context window management: what to include, what to summarize
Conversation history strategies for multi-turn apps
Prompt caching — how it works, when it saves money
Injecting dynamic context safely
Token counting before you send
Long document handling patterns
exam_gotcha: Prompt caching requires the cached prefix to be identical byte-for-byte. Even a single space difference breaks the cache. Always put stable content (system prompts, long docs) at the top.
key_concept: Prompt caching can reduce costs by up to 90% for repeated prefixes — critical for production cost optimization.

quiz_questions.q: Where should stable, reused content be placed to benefit from prompt caching?
quiz_questions.a: At the beginning of the prompt (before dynamic content)

quiz_questions.q: What API feature lets you count tokens before making a full request?
quiz_questions.a: The token counting API / count_tokens endpoint

quiz_questions.q: What must be true for a prompt cache hit to occur?
quiz_questions.a: The prefix must be byte-for-byte identical to the previously cached prompt

quiz_questions.q: What strategy helps manage context in long multi-turn conversations?
quiz_questions.a: Summarizing older turns and replacing them with a compressed summary

title: Tool Use & Function Calling
tagline: Give Claude hands, not just a mind
subtopics: Tool definition schema — name, description, input_schema
Single tool vs parallel tool use
Tool result handling and the tool_result content block
Forcing tool use with tool_choice parameter
Building reliable tool descriptions (this is where most failures happen)
Error handling when tools fail
Computer use tools — special capabilities and risks
exam_gotcha: tool_choice: {type: 'tool', name: 'my_tool'} forces a specific tool. tool_choice: {type: 'any'} forces Claude to use at least one tool. Without tool_choice, Claude decides.
key_concept: Tool descriptions are prompts — Claude decides whether and how to use a tool based entirely on the description. Vague descriptions = unreliable tool use.

quiz_questions.q: What content block type do you use to return tool results to Claude?
quiz_questions.a: tool_result content block

quiz_questions.q: How do you force Claude to use a specific tool?
quiz_questions.a: Set tool_choice to {type: 'tool', name: 'tool_name'}

quiz_questions.q: Can Claude call multiple tools in a single response?
quiz_questions.a: Yes — parallel tool use allows multiple tool calls in one turn

quiz_questions.q: What schema format is used to define tool input parameters?
quiz_questions.a: JSON Schema

title: Multi-Agent Architecture
tagline: One Claude is powerful. Many Claudes, coordinated, are transformative.
subtopics: Orchestrator vs subagent roles
When to use multi-agent vs single-agent
Trust levels: how much to trust subagent output
Passing context between agents efficiently
Preventing prompt injection through agent chains
Parallelization patterns for speed
Failure handling and retry logic in agent networks
exam_gotcha: Subagents should be treated as untrusted by default — a compromised subagent (via prompt injection in retrieved content) can poison an orchestrator. Always validate subagent outputs.
key_concept: Multi-agent is not always better. Use it when: tasks are too long for one context window, tasks benefit from parallelism, or independent verification adds value.

quiz_questions.q: What role directs other agents and synthesizes results?
quiz_questions.a: Orchestrator

quiz_questions.q: Why should orchestrators treat subagent outputs with skepticism?
quiz_questions.a: Subagents may have processed untrusted content that injected malicious instructions

quiz_questions.q: Name two scenarios where multi-agent architecture is clearly beneficial.
quiz_questions.a: Tasks exceeding one context window; tasks that can run in parallel to save time

quiz_questions.q: What is the main risk of blindly passing subagent output to the next agent?
quiz_questions.a: Prompt injection — malicious content in retrieved data can hijack the agent chain

title: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
subtopics: What MCP is and why it exists
MCP server vs MCP client architecture
Three primitives: Tools, Resources, Prompts
Transport types: stdio vs SSE
Writing an MCP server from scratch
Security considerations for MCP servers
MCP in Claude Desktop vs Claude Code vs API
exam_gotcha: MCP has three primitives — Tools (actions Claude can call), Resources (data Claude can read), and Prompts (reusable prompt templates). Confusing these is a common exam mistake.
key_concept: MCP standardizes how AI models connect to external data and tools — one protocol, any integration. Think of it as an API standard for AI context.

quiz_questions.q: What are the three MCP primitives?
quiz_questions.a: Tools, Resources, and Prompts

quiz_questions.q: What does MCP stand for?
quiz_questions.a: Model Context Protocol

quiz_questions.q: What are the two transport types supported by MCP?
quiz_questions.a: stdio (standard input/output) and SSE (Server-Sent Events)

quiz_questions.q: In MCP, what primitive provides reusable prompt templates?
quiz_questions.a: Prompts

title: RAG, Memory & Knowledge Patterns
tagline: Claude's knowledge ends at training. RAG makes it limitless.
subtopics: RAG architecture — retrieval, augmentation, generation
Chunking strategies and why they matter
Embedding models and vector databases
Reranking for precision
Memory types: in-context, external, episodic, semantic
When to use RAG vs fine-tuning vs prompt stuffing
Handling retrieval failures gracefully
exam_gotcha: RAG vs fine-tuning: RAG is for dynamic, updatable knowledge. Fine-tuning is for style/behavior change. Most production knowledge retrieval should use RAG, not fine-tuning.
key_concept: Chunk size is one of the most impactful RAG tuning decisions — too small loses context, too large reduces precision. 512-1024 tokens with overlap is a common starting point.

quiz_questions.q: What does RAG stand for?
quiz_questions.a: Retrieval-Augmented Generation

quiz_questions.q: When should you prefer RAG over fine-tuning?
quiz_questions.a: When knowledge needs to be dynamic, updatable, or traceable to sources

quiz_questions.q: What does a reranker do in a RAG pipeline?
quiz_questions.a: Re-scores retrieved chunks for relevance before passing them to the model

quiz_questions.q: What type of memory persists between sessions in an external database?
quiz_questions.a: External memory (also called persistent or long-term memory)

title: Safety, Guardrails & Responsible AI
tagline: Building powerful AI means building safe AI
subtopics: Constitutional AI — how Claude's values are trained
Harm categories Claude won't assist with
Jailbreak patterns and why they (mostly) don't work on Claude
Input and output filtering strategies
Content moderation architecture
The Responsible Scaling Policy (RSP)
How to handle policy edge cases in your application
exam_gotcha: Claude's refusals come from trained values, not a keyword blocklist. You cannot bypass them by rephrasing — this is by design. Exam questions often test whether you understand this distinction.
key_concept: Constitutional AI trains Claude to critique and revise its own outputs against a set of principles — it's not post-hoc filtering, it's baked into training.

quiz_questions.q: What training methodology gives Claude its safety behaviors?
quiz_questions.a: Constitutional AI (CAI)

quiz_questions.q: Is Claude's refusal behavior based on keyword matching?
quiz_questions.a: No — it's based on trained values and understanding of intent, not keywords

quiz_questions.q: What is Anthropic's policy for scaling model capabilities safely?
quiz_questions.a: The Responsible Scaling Policy (RSP)

quiz_questions.q: What are Claude's 'hardcoded' behaviors?
quiz_questions.a: Absolute limits that cannot be changed by any operator or user prompt — e.g., no CSAM, no bioweapons assistance

title: Production Architecture: Cost, Latency & Streaming
tagline: A great AI product is useless if it's slow or unaffordable
subtopics: Streaming responses with SSE — why and how
Batch API for async, high-volume workloads
Cost optimization strategies: caching, model selection, prompt compression
Latency optimization: streaming, model choice, parallel calls
Monitoring and observability for AI systems
Token budget management at scale
Fallback strategies when the API is unavailable
exam_gotcha: The Batch API offers 50% cost reduction but adds latency (responses within 24 hours). It's for async workloads — never for real-time user-facing interactions.
key_concept: Streaming (SSE) doesn't reduce total latency — it reduces perceived latency by showing output as it generates. Time-to-first-token matters more than total time for UX.

quiz_questions.q: What API feature reduces cost by ~50% for non-real-time workloads?
quiz_questions.a: The Batch API (Message Batches API)

quiz_questions.q: Does streaming reduce total response generation time?
quiz_questions.a: No — it reduces perceived latency by surfacing tokens as they're generated

quiz_questions.q: What metric matters most for user-perceived AI response speed?
quiz_questions.a: Time-to-first-token (TTFT)

quiz_questions.q: Name two strategies to reduce Claude API costs in production.
quiz_questions.a: Prompt caching, using smaller models (Haiku) for simpler tasks, Batch API for async work

exam_gotcha: The exam tests architecture judgment, not just API knowledge. Questions often present a scenario and ask which approach is BEST — knowing tradeoffs beats memorizing facts.
key_concept: Architect-level thinking: always consider cost, latency, safety, and maintainability together. No single dimension wins.

quiz_questions.q: A user needs Claude to analyze 500 documents overnight. Which API feature is ideal?
quiz_questions.a: Batch API (Message Batches) — async, 50% cheaper, no real-time requirement

quiz_questions.q: Your chatbot's context window fills up after 20 turns. What's the best strategy?
quiz_questions.a: Summarize older turns and replace them with a compressed summary in context

quiz_questions.q: An operator wants to prevent Claude from discussing competitors. Where should this instruction go?
quiz_questions.a: The system prompt — operators control Claude's behavior via system prompts

quiz_questions.q: What's the safest way to let Claude browse the web?
quiz_questions.a: Tool use with a controlled web search tool — never give Claude raw browser access without sandboxing
